The harness's own scanSources reads it as UTF-8 and sees the declaration fine; `grep -a` finds it too.

chose: fix sources=[src,test] + testDir='test/' — adopting the atlas exposed that the sidecar scan was reading the wrong population
over: keeping sources=[src], testDir='test' and marking runNamedTest knownPending to make atlas --check green
because: MEASURED: scanSources splits by `rel.includes(testDir)`, so testDir='test' matched src/run-named-test.ts and src/test-batch.ts — two modules deliberately moved INSIDE the evidence perimeter — and pushed them out of the scanned `src`. atlas graded runNamedTest DANGLING for it. Worse, sources=['src'] meant the real test tree was never scanned at all, so conventions' totalityTests set was those two misclassified files: the ORACLE grade was structurally unreachable in this repo, and every guard could only ever come back CONVENTION or single. Now src=54 / test=42 (was 52 / 2).

chose: chart coherence's atlas over EVIDENCE trust domains (project-source · derived-model · shell · record · verdict · reading-surface), not over network/authz zones

charting the source tree's own module layers, which would restate the graph
because: the atlas's semantics are 'trust domains + chokepoints that RE-ESTABLISH the destination's invariant', and coherence's scarce resource is not privilege but WARRANT: what a gate is permitted to say. All 14 spec boundary chokepoints land as crossings with zero non-transitions — the whole codebase is the seam between a repo and a verdict — and the charting immediately paid: 3 tier-3 SECURITY crossings with no boundary claim at all (buildGraph, loadConfig, readJsonOrRefuse), the three ingress doors nothing in the spec governs.

chose: contracts: NOT APPLICABLE to coherence — one path-addressable deploy unit, so cfg.artifacts has nothing to partition
over: declaring the render-side embedded browser scripts as a second artifact
leaving `contracts` unconfigured and silent, which is indistinguishable from never having considered it
because: MEASURED: package.json ships one compile unit (tsc over src/ → dist/cli.js + dist/hook-cli.js from the same run), so every symbol resolves to the same artifact and `cross` is structurally false. The genuine cross-unit seam DOES exist — 6 <script> blocks across render-contract/-index/-outline, whose Node producers hand data to browser consumers nothing typechecks (render-contract JSON.parses an embedded PromiseModel; render-index/-outline read data-* attributes) — but cfg.artifacts partitions by PATH GLOB and both sides of each seam live in ONE file, as a template literal. The mechanism cannot address it. Declaring it anyway would also fail --check as UNANCHORED, since no boundary claim names `embed` or the payload type. Re-run the query by counting compile units in package.json + <script> blocks in src/render-*.ts; if the browser scripts are ever extracted to their own files this answer flips.

chose: leave cfg.artifacts UNSET rather than declaring the single unit `cli: [src/**]` to make contracts say something
over: declaring one artifact so the gate reports a measurement instead of silence
because: MEASURED by trying it: with one artifact declared, `contracts` prints '✓ every cross-artifact shared file is covered by a declared contract or an anchored claim' and exits 0 — a CHECKMARK over a population that is empty by construction (no two artifacts, so no importer set can be disjoint). That is 0-of-0 rendering as 0-of-500, the precise defect floor.ts's header forbids, and it is worse than the unconfigured message ('no contracts/artifacts config — nothing to check'), which at least admits it measured nothing. The gate has no floor of its own: a project with one deploy unit gets an unearned green from `contracts --check` today.

chose: could not leave `premise --check` green — it FAILS on pristine v0.25.0 too, so CI on main is red today and was before this work
because: The single gate-grade failure is d-d31f0a5a, whose `chose` records EVICTING src/scene.ts and src/render-scene.ts. Its strong lease therefore names the files the decision deleted, and can never resolve again: a decision that records a deletion is structurally unable to keep its premise. The two remedies the tool prints are both wrong here — `retract` means 'what refuted it' and nothing refuted it (it was carried out), and a replacement decision does not clear the original's lease. Fixing it needs either a premise-side rule that a lease on a path the SAME decision says it deleted is satisfied-by-deletion, or an explicit 'executed' terminal state distinct from retraction. Not mine to invent inside a gate-adoption job. Side effect worth noting: pinning mass-baseline.json cleared one of the 20 ADVISORY missing-address findings (d-cfa92038 named it), so adoption moved the number in the right direction.

chose: report the Index figure's first overflow on a second shape rather than fix the geometry inside a gate-adoption job
over: widening main's 1184px content column, or shrinking the lattice column tracks, to make the spine fit
because: MEASURED on two live shapes now. hoist: 4 spine stages, 9 column tracks at 112/128px, fgrid width 968px — fits the 1184px content column with room to spare, which is why five design rounds never saw this. coherence: 5 spine stages, 11 tracks at 128/144px (longer chart names — project-source, derived-model, reading-surface), fgrid width 1368px — it OVERFLOWS by ~230px. It degrades correctly (.figure is overflow-x:auto, so it scrolls and nothing is lost) but the default view cuts the spine's TERMINAL stage, `verdict`, which is the box the whole figure is about, and there is no affordance saying it scrolls. Figure width is a function of (spine stages x label length) and crosses the column at 5 stages of ~15 chars. That is the second dataset the MAP figure never had; the fix wants a design judgment, not a same-session patch.
